properties.name: BUILT — nine tools bounded through ONE shared helper, with a CI gate that fails when nothing overflowed. Two tools are exempt as documents, and the first version's own bug is pinned by a test
properties.statement:
BUILT 2026-09-13, answering fact:the-unbounded-reply-sweep-2026-09-13 as a CLASS rather than as the one tool it was reported from.

WHAT LANDED: crates/reflow2-mcp/src/reply_budget.rs — one helper, not a fourth bespoke trimmer. Prose is cut progressively (4000, 2000, 800, 240, 120, 0 characters); numbers, counts and ids are never touched; every trimmed reply carries a `budget` block saying what went and how to get it back.

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, on this design seeded into a fresh store:

    describe_schema        117,252 ->  47,904   (all 65 edge types still listed)
    confirmation_ledger    125,383 ->  31,673
    invalidated_findings    88,242 ->  27,492
    evidence_report          75,159 ->  18,643
    detect_defects           56,455 ->  31,971
    compare_designs        9-16 MB  ->  bounded (the originally reported friction)
    list_skills, export_surface, get_instructions — see below

⚠️ THREE STILL LAND A FEW PERCENT OVER THE 30,000 DEFAULT, and that is the honest trade rather than a miss: once prose is gone what remains is STRUCTURE — ids, counts, keys — which this helper will not trim because trimming it is what makes a shorter answer a quieter one. Each reply reports its own `reply_chars`, so the residual is visible and not claimed away.

🛑 TWO TOOLS ARE EXEMPT AND THE EXEMPTION IS THE INTERESTING PART. get_instructions and export_surface return DOCUMENTS, not reports. Character-trimming one is corrupt rather than short — half an instruction set reads exactly like a whole one. Worse, get_instructions already tells its reader "if `instructions` is shorter than `returned_bytes`, YOUR CLIENT CAPPED IT", a signal added after a real consumer lost the back half twice, nine days apart: trimming there would have made the tool accuse the client of reflow2's own edit. Both now WITHHOLD WHOLE over budget and hand back the narrower call that works (`section`, `path`). export_graph stays excluded for the same reason.

⭐ THE FIRST VERSION OF THE HELPER HAD THE EXACT BUG IT EXISTS TO PREVENT, and a committed test caught it within the hour: capping lists for every caller returned ONE of describe_schema's 65 edge types, still shaped like a complete vocabulary. Shortening a LIST is now opt-in (`Sampling::Allowed`) and the default is Forbidden — over budget, such a tool overflows LOUDLY rather than going quiet. A `NEVER_TRIM_BELOW` floor of 80 characters is what makes the 0 rung safe: names, ids and enum values survive every rung, so a vocabulary comes back complete and terse instead of complete and empty. Both behaviours are pinned by their own tests.

⭐ THE DETECTOR, which is the leg that was missing. tools/replies_are_bounded.py runs in CI: it SEEDS a real design from the committed export, calls every no-argument read tool, and fails if any reply exceeds the budget without declaring a bound. Toolsnaps could never catch this — a golden pins the tools that EXIST, so a NEW tool returning 126 KB unbounded is a clean diff and a green build.

🛑 AND IT FAILS WHEN IT HAD NOTHING TO RUN ON. If no reply overflowed, the gate EXITS 1 rather than passing, because on an empty graph every reply is small and it would pass having checked nothing. "No tool overflowed" and "I could not make any tool overflow" must not share an exit code. VERIFIED TO FAIL, not merely to pass: at --budget 5000 it exits 1 and names eight unbounded tools.

📌 THOSE EIGHT ARE A STANDING LIST, not a clean bill: design_regions, evaluate_allocation, granularity_report, graph_report, ility_report, manual_work_report, reviewed_defects and surprising_connections all sit under 30,000 on THIS design and would cross on a larger one. The gate will fail the day they do, which is the point of having it.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: only the 37 no-argument read tools are swept, so the 143 requiring arguments remain unmeasured apart from compare_designs. Sizes are for this design. The tool DESCRIPTIONS were not rewritten to mention the bound — the `budget_chars` parameter description carries it instead, which is a weaker instruction leg than the three original tools have.
